title: Targeted signal perturbation propagated to clinical variant-call loss
finding: In the controlled HG002 F11 case, targeted PM2 perturbation reduced evaluable ALT-supporting parents from 14/14 in the clean condition to 0/14 on target, with downstream loss of the clinically relevant F11 variant call.
limitation: Single HG002 individual, one pathogenic F11 locus and one basecaller/perturbation configuration; no patient outcome was observed.

title: The demonstrated F11 chain reached maximal score on its applicable dimensions
finding: The F11 experimental case scored D2=1.0 and D7=1.0 because the tested perturbation completely suppressed evaluable allele evidence and propagated through the observed S2->S4->S5 clinical-processing chain.
limitation: This is a case-level computational severity score, not a probability of clinical harm.

title: Genomic disclosure remained highly persistent in the B2 model
finding: The authoritative B2 model produced pathogenic-variant unrecoverability of 0.2299, 100% modelled re-identification by year 13 and 100% modelled familial exposure by year 15.
limitation: These are model-derived trajectories rather than observed longitudinal population outcomes.

title: Kinship structure substantially amplified exposure
finding: The authoritative B1 analysis used a 4,144-node graph with 1,657 registered nodes and produced calibrated mean familial amplification of 464.4x, corresponding to D6=0.898.
limitation: Amplification remains dependent on graph construction and calibration assumptions.

title: The integrated privacy chain produced a high Base GRI
finding: Across applicable privacy dimensions D1, D3, D5 and D6, the authoritative Base GRI was 0.9373875000.
limitation: The score combines model-derived dimensions and should not be interpreted as an empirical population probability.

title: Privacy risk remained high under provenance-balanced weighting
finding: When B2-derived dimensions were collapsed into one composite and weighted 50/50 against B1 amplification, the privacy sensitivity score remained high.
limitation: Sensitivity analysis is a robustness check and is not a confidence interval.

title: Containment effectiveness depended strongly on attack origin
finding: B3 containment achieved 99.24% best reduction in the primary scenario, but fixed-k residual containment difficulty varied substantially by attack origin.
quantitative_anchor: M5 residual candidates at k=10: peripheral=0.008; mid-degree=0.795; hub=0.970
limitation: M5 values are scenario-specific residual candidates and are not multiplied into Base GRI.

title: Authentication is mitigation context rather than privacy detectability
finding: The final B3 credential-stuffing benchmark used threshold 3.6 and achieved F1=0.8387, but this performance is treated as access-control mitigation evidence rather than a direct measure of privacy-event detectability.
limitation: Internal generated benchmark; M3 detectability remains UNMEASURED.

title: A1 and A2 strengthen lifecycle coverage without inflating GRI
finding: A1 contributes standalone software-security evidence and A2 contributes supporting perturbation evidence, but neither is forced into the Base GRI where the required semantic mapping is not established.
limitation: Their exclusion from Base GRI is deliberate and should not be interpreted as lack of scientific relevance.
